chapter_title: Concerning the Seed Grain that shall be formed by
spiritual_reading:
¶2 — Seeds, grains, elements, warmth/cold, nourishment vs hunger/destruction.
The “seed grain” and “barley grain” correspond to interior truths in potency (a seed contains the whole future form), specifically truths for the natural degree that can be made serviceable to spiritual life. “Barley” (a staple grain) points to truth that feeds the outer person—knowledges and simple goods that sustain the natural mind. Their being “formed” and “beautified by the five elements” describes how influx descends and is clothed in ultimates: the inner truth (spiritual degree) takes on determinate natural forms through the ordered conditions of the natural world (elements = the general receptacles and states of the natural mind in which spiritual things terminate).

“Warmth and cold” are the alternating states by which life is regulated in the natural: warmth corresponds to love/affection (the will’s heat), and cold to the lack or remission of that love (a state of obscurity or withdrawal in the will). Together they “nourish the seed grain and the entire tree” because regeneration in ultimates proceeds by alternations—states of affection and states of comparative non-affection—by which the natural is disciplined and made receptive. The “tree” is the full formed perception and life from that seed: a system of thought and conduct growing from implanted truth.

But the same natural conditions that sustain can also, in the opposite sense, become occasions of perversion: when the connection to the higher degrees is cut, nourishment becomes “hunger,” and the seed and tree are “destroyed.” Spiritually, “hunger” is deprivation of good and truth—an emptied natural mind that no longer receives influx from above, so that what was capable of becoming living truth becomes barren and collapses.

¶4 — Lack/shortfall from place to place; choosing, gathering, beautifying, attaining; then affliction through those.
A “lack and shortfall…from place to place” describes an uneven reception of influx across the mind’s provinces (places = states and regions of life in the Grand Human). When order is disturbed in ultimates, the deficiency is not universal in the same way; it varies according to state—here more reception, there less—producing spiritual imbalance.

“They who have chosen it” indicates the turning of the will: choice is the appropriation of a state. To “gather it in” is to collect and store knowledges and appearances of truth in the memory (natural degree), and to “beautify” is to arrange externals so they appear fair and persuasive—an external adornment of doctrine and life. To “attain it” is to make it one’s possession, so that it becomes habitual in the outer person.

Yet “an affliction shall arise for it through those” reveals the spiritual law that what is merely gathered and adorned in the natural, without being vivified from the spiritual and celestial degrees, becomes the occasion of infestation: affliction = temptation/pressures and also the distress that comes when externals are assaulted by contrary influx. In the opposite sense, those same gathered-and-adorned things become instruments by which disorder attacks what could have been living—external truths turned into means for falsity and self-justification, producing spiritual oppression.

¶5 — Stumbling; energy of Matter dwelling in them; shadow poured over people and elements; destruction of fruits.
To “stumble” corresponds to a fall in understanding and life—an interruption of spiritual walking (progression in order). The cause is “the energy of Matter that dwells in them”: Matter, in this teaching layer, functions as the principle of the merely natural severed from higher influx—natural desire and inertial force when it is not subordinate. Its “energy” is the active push of the lowest degree when it rebels against the higher (the natural striving to rule), which Swedenborg would describe as the proprium acting from self-love and the world.

This Matter “pours its shadow” over them: a “shadow” is obscurity and falsification—darkness not simply from ignorance but from an interposed veil that blocks light. In correspondences, light is truth/wisdom; shadow is its deprivation in the understanding. When shadow is poured over “the elements,” it signifies that even the general receptacles of the natural mind (the elemental conditions by which truths are formed in ultimates) are darkened; thus the whole process by which seeds become trees in the natural is corrupted.

Therefore it “destroys the fruits of all the trees.” “Fruits” are the goods of life—works, uses, and the delights of good that are the end of truths. “Trees” are perceptions and doctrinal forms; their fruits are the actual good that should proceed. When shadow rules, the end is lost: truths (seeds/trees) may remain as forms, but their goods (fruits) perish.

Continuous spiritual narrative.
The chapter describes how interior truths meant to feed and build the outer person (seed and barley) descend into formation in the natural degree through the general conditions of ultimate life (elements), and how regeneration there requires alternations of affection and its remission (warmth and cold) to nourish both the implanted beginnings and their developed forms (tree). But when higher influx is withheld or rejected, those same ultimates experience spiritual “hunger,” and the formed life is destroyed.

From this severing arises an uneven deficiency across one’s states (“place to place”): people choose and appropriate externals, gather them into memory, and adorn them so they appear complete, even attaining them as possessions; yet because they are not vivified from within, infestation follows—affliction arises through the very externals relied upon. Finally, the rebellious activity of the merely natural (Matter’s energy) induces stumbling: it spreads a shadow that blocks spiritual light in the understanding, darkens even the natural receptacles by which truth should be made living, and so cuts off the final purpose of all truth—good in act—by destroying the fruits of the trees. In this way the text traces the downward logic of disorder: from seeds meant for nourishment, to deprivation, to uneven lack, to external appropriation without life, to obscuring falsity that makes the natural rule, and thus to the loss of goods that are the ends of spiritual growth.

fills.notes: After “shall be formed and … and beautified,” the substrate logic requires the intermediate step of development from potency to actuality: seed → growth → adornment/ordering in ultimates by the elements. “Grown” fits the natural correspondence (increase/extension in the natural degree) without introducing later paraenetic language.

The clause compares nourishing conditions to their opposite outcome when order is inverted. A transitional formula is demanded: as warmth/cold nourish in alternations, so (in the opposite sense) they can occasion ruin. “in turn, so too” keeps the impersonal, instructional register of the oldest layer.

fills.fill: when its root is cut off from the living influx
fills.notes: The destruction is not from the elements themselves but from severance from the higher degree (the ‘root’ correspondence: interior conjunction that supplies life to the natural). This supplies the missing condition that turns nourishment into deprivation, matching the chapter’s spiritual narrative of higher influx withheld/rejected.

The final phrase must yield “through the state of hunger,” i.e., deprivation as a state of reception, not merely a bodily image. This preserves the correspondential sense (hunger = lack of good/truth in the natural mind) in the oldest, descriptive register.

assessment: All four lacunae can be restored in a way that matches the correspondential sequence (formation → growth → beautification; nourishment by alternations; inversion through severance; destruction through a state of deprivation). Exact connective particles are less constrained than the underlying spiritual logic, so confidence is strongest on the semantic roles and weaker on the precise phrasing of the transition/condition.
